title: 1963 AHSME Problem 9
statement: In the expansion of \(\left(a-\dfrac1{\sqrt a}\right)^7\) the coefficient of \(a^{-\frac{1}{2}}\) is:

solutions.text:
The term using \(-a^{-\frac{1}{2}}\) exactly \(r\) times has exponent \(7-r-\frac{r}{2}=7-\frac{3r}{2}.\) Setting this to \(-\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(r=5.\) Its coefficient is \(\binom75(-1)^5=-21.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: The term choosing the second summand \(r\) times has exponent \(7-\frac{3r}{2}\)
Set that exponent equal to \(-\frac{1}{2}\) before finding the binomial coefficient and sign
